read.thesis: UPS shrinks its US network to exit Amazon volume: Q4 US ADV down 10.8% but revenue per piece up 8.3%, with 2026 guided at ~9.6% consolidated margin and H1 pressure before H2 recovery.

capex.quote: Capital expenditures are expected to be about $3 billion.

triggers.label: 93 buildings closed, 57 automated in 2025
triggers.quote: We closed 93 buildings in the U.S. and deployed automation in 57 buildings while maintaining the high level of service our customers expect.

triggers.label: US revenue per piece +8.3% in Q4
triggers.quote: In the fourth quarter, revenue per piece increased 8.3% year over year, which was the strongest fourth quarter revenue per piece growth rate we've seen in four years.

triggers.label: US ADV down 10.8% in Q4
triggers.quote: total U.S. average daily volume was down 2.4 million pieces or 10.8%.

triggers.label: Q1 international profit down ~30%
triggers.quote: We expect profit to be down about 30% in the first quarter and then recover as we go throughout the year.

guidance.quote: we expect to generate consolidated revenue of approximately $89.7 billion and a consolidated operating margin of approximately 9.6%
a consolidated operating margin of approximately 9.6%
Capital expenditures are expected to be about $3 billion.
We expect free cash flow to be approximately $6.5 billion
we are targeting $3 billion in savings related to the Amazon glide down.
Full year operating margin is expected to be flat to 2025.

prior_guidance_check.quote: By the end of the year, we reached our volume reduction target and reduced Amazon's volume in our network by approximately 1 million pieces per day.
As planned, we delivered $3.5 billion in savings from our network reconfiguration and efficiency reimagined initiatives.

red_flags.label: H1 2026 margin pressure and cost lag
red_flags.quote: We know that variable costs come out as volume exits the network, but I have learned that reductions in fixed and semi-variable costs lag.

red_flags.label: Cost per piece up 8.9% in Q4
red_flags.quote: Cost per piece increased 8.9% year over year, primarily due to costs associated with the insourcing of Groundsaver

evasions.quote: let us get through this year, 2026 is the pivotal year for United Parcel Service, Inc.
